draft.title: Contact and conflict at Sydney Cove
card: In 1788 the British set up a colony at Sydney Cove. The Sydney region was already home to Aboriginal clans, including the Eora and the Darug.
The British cleared land, built farms and took fish and game. This cut Aboriginal people off from places and food sources they had cared for over many generations.
Aboriginal people did not accept this. They resisted in different ways, including by defending their land and taking food from colonial farms.
Pemulwuy, a Bidjigal man, led attacks on colonists for over a decade. The British saw him as a threat and he was killed in 1802.
draft.remember: The colony took land and food, and Aboriginal people, such as Pemulwuy, resisted.

a.q: Why did conflict begin around Sydney Cove after 1788?
opts: The colony took land and food Aboriginal people relied on
Aboriginal clans wanted to trade for British farming tools
Aboriginal clans moved onto land the British had farmed
The British would not share their food with Aboriginal people
a.why: The British cleared land and took fish and game, so Aboriginal people lost places and food they relied on. The land was already home to Aboriginal clans, so it was not the case that they moved onto British farms.
a.clue: Think about who was living around the cove before 1788.

b.q: Which statement best describes Pemulwuy's role in the conflict around Sydney?
opts: He led resistance by a Bidjigal man for over a decade
He was a British governor who ordered farms to be built
He was a Darug trader who sold food to the colony
He led a short revolt that ended within a few months
b.why: Pemulwuy, a Bidjigal man, led attacks on colonists for over a decade, so his resistance was long, not short. He was an Aboriginal leader, not a governor or a trader supplying the colony.
b.clue: Remember how long his attacks went on.
